plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration limit.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a stable, low-drawdown portfolio with a focus on income and broad index exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets a modest ~1.5%/month return potential, prioritizing capital preservation. Expect lower volatility and reduced drawdown risk, but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL) to small positions.

This plan balances growth with risk management, maintaining some exposure to quality tech.
It aims for a blend of broad index, income, and reduced leveraged exposure.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5%/month return potential, focusing on risk-first growth. It aims for a moderate risk profile with a blend of broad market and quality tech exposure.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration limit.

aggressive.read: This aggressive approach targets ~4%/month return potential, stretching for growth. It involves significant leverage and concentration, leading to higher potential drawdowns and daily decay from leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.

income.read: This income approach targets ~1%/month return potential, focusing on yield and capital preservation. Expect lower growth potential and note that distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
